evidence: Action buttons (jog/home, START TEST PRINT, START SYSTEM, START PRINT) have no confirmation toast, checkmark, loading state, or state change after click. User cannot confirm action executed successfully. Reference standard: 'Completed actions confirm (state change, toast, checkmark) — the user never wonders "did it work?"'
recommendation: Add immediate feedback for action buttons: show loading state (spinner/disabled button) during action, then success toast on completion. Example flow: button click → 'Homing X...' (loading) → 'Homing complete' (toast).

evidence: Red error toast 'FluidNC Telnet offline: 10.28.8.74:23; HTTP offline (timed out)' displays failure message but no recovery path. No retry button, reconnect action, or diagnostic guidance. Reference standard: 'Failures show a recoverable error state (message + retry), not a crash, blank screen, or silent nothing.'
recommendation: Provide recovery options in error state: add 'Retry' button to reconnect, or include diagnostic guidance: 'Check FluidNC controller is powered on and connected to network (IP: 10.28.8.74).' Make error actionable, not terminal.

evidence: Error toast has no dismiss mechanism (no close button, X, or explicit acknowledgment path). Toast persists indefinitely on screen, blocking visual real estate. User cannot acknowledge they've seen the error.
recommendation: Add close button (X) to error toast. Alternatively, implement auto-dismiss after 5–8 seconds with re-show if condition persists, so error doesn't clutter UI indefinitely.

evidence: Error state is inconsistent across workflow tabs. Red FluidNC offline toast is visible in screens 03–04 (mid-workflow) but absent in screens 05–06, despite error condition persisting (dry-run, no controller). Operator navigates through tabs; error disappears and reappears unpredictably, breaking confidence in system state clarity. Violates FLOW-4: 'Errors mid-flow are recoverable without restarting the flow.'
recommendation: Ensure error state persists visibly across all tabs until user explicitly dismisses it. If toast must auto-dismiss (UI best practice: 5–8s), re-show it if error condition is still active when user returns to that section. Provide persistent indicator (icon/badge on tab or status area) if error is blocking workflow.
